video_title: 'The most severe punishment given out in NBA history!' - Shams on Kawhi & Clippers' investigation 👀

quotes.speaker: Pat McAfee
quotes.summary_phrase: Pat McAfee questions the timing of the NBA investigation into the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: It feels like in this particular case, something happened that Adam Silver was not happy about.
quotes.quote: We know Steve Ballmer is a character. It feels like in this particular case, something happened that Adam Silver was not happy about at all. There was a report at one point that there was nothing found, then the NBA was like, 'Nope, that's not true at all.' There was a trade of Kawhi Leonard to Toronto that was supposed to happen, and the NBA said, 'Nope, you should probably wait until we're done with our investigation.' Did we know that the investigation was coming to a point at this time, and what really does this all say about the situation?

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania details the complexity of the NBA investigation into the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: Adam Silver is the judge, he's the jury, he's got the final word.
quotes.quote: What this says is this is the most severe punishment given out in American pro sports. That's for sure. And what this does say at the end of it is, above all, Adam Silver is the judge, he's the jury, he's got the final word. The NBA had Wachtell, Lipton, a third-party law firm, basically commissioned as the investigator, the lead investigator for this last September. And then they published that 36-page report yesterday on Wednesday. My understanding is back in late July, the Clippers already received all of the findings that the NBA had from Wachtell, Lipton on all the charges, all the emails, all the text messages, everything that they've got here in this 36-page report. Things always come up at the last second, there's always more information, this is always fluid. That's what goes into these types of investigations. There's all these different sides, right? It's the Clippers, it's Steve Ballmer, it's Steve Ballmer's lawyers, it's the Clippers' lawyers, it's the NBA, it's Adam Silver, it's the lawyers at the league, it's the Wachtell, Lipton lawyers as well. And then there's the whole Kawhi Leonard, then his agent, then his former business rep, then the union representatives. There's all these people, there's all these sides, so these are complex stories, no question.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on improper team introductions to players and sponsors
quotes.excerpt: Teams in the NBA are allowed to make introductions to their players and sponsors.
quotes.quote: At the crux of this is the introductions that the NBA found that rose to the level of not just normal introductions that teams make. Teams in the NBA are allowed to make introductions to their players and sponsors. Any individual player, likely 60 to 70 percent of their sponsors are coming directly with the team sponsors just because it's in-house. Well, you can introduce a player, like the Clippers could have introduced Kawhi Leonard to Dactronics or any of these other four companies that they've been found to basically brokering these deals. The issue here is that there is proof at least on one occasion, Gillian Zucker, the president of business, who got suspended for a full year, well she, according to the NBA's findings, negotiated a deal in the millions with a company and a middleman, the middle agent, for Kawhi Leonard on behalf of Kawhi Leonard before it even reached the point of an introduction.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on the Clippers acting as a power agent
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers basically acted as some form of a power agent for Kawhi Leonard in some instances.
quotes.quote: When I talked to team executives last night, one mentioned to me, the Clippers basically acted as some form of a power agent for Kawhi Leonard in some instances. And that's where it rises from just introductions or just an innocent situation to, okay, there is some intent here on circumventing the salary cap. Cases like that are why when I talk to team executives last night, one mentioned to me, the Clippers basically acted as some form of a power agent for Kawhi Leonard in some instances. And that's where it rises from just introductions or just an innocent situation to, okay, there is some intent here on circumventing the salary cap.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on the timing of the Clippers' deals
quotes.excerpt: These deals were being inked and discussed and talked about during 2020 and 2021.
quotes.quote: I don't know why anyone involved in this situation managed these deals the way they did. To have deals in the tens of millions of dollars of range, Kawhi Leonard, these deals were being inked and discussed and talked about during 2020 and 2021. This is during the COVID pandemic when businesses were basically at times using COVID and the pandemic and that was around the country as a reason why businesses were actually suffering, that money wasn't as available. I talk to agents and players now, these endorsement deals were not hot and popping during COVID times in 2020 and 2021, but for some reason, Kawhi Leonard was getting tens of millions of dollars in endorsement deals and by mid-2021, he had already pocketed over $10 million dollars in endorsement deals with basically no obligation.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on the lack of proof regarding Kawhi Leonard's knowledge
quotes.excerpt: There was no evidence there that showed that he had knowledge or he first-hand worked on circumventing.
quotes.quote: The NBA did publish that report with Wachtell, Lipton 36 pages. There was no evidence there that showed that he had knowledge or he first-hand worked on circumventing the salary cap. Basically Dennis Robertson, the uncle, had all the power, had all the say so, is just like Adam Silver does with the NBA, Dennis Robertson and everyone around the NBA knows it, he ran Kawhi Leonard, he ran his life. And so, when you talk to people around the players union, it's, they're using this as a cautionary tale of what can happen when someone has this much power around you and you're the player.
